title: Regional queueing outreach template for partners
body:
Purpose:
This document is a concise, partner-facing update and template for outreach when a regional request queueing condition causes elevated end-to-end latency and sporadic throttling for a subset of customers. The goal is to give partner-facing teams (account management, partner operations, and support) a ready-to-send message, a short technical summary, suggested mitigations, and a post-incident follow-up plan that maps to our SLA and remediation commitments.

When to use this template:
- Observed request queueing in a single region or restricted availability zone causing sustained latency degradation (>2x baseline) or increased client timeouts for >5% of requests over a rolling 10-minute window.
- Impact limited to hosted inference endpoints or routing tier affecting partner integrations.
- No active data loss or corruption confirmed.

Audience:
- Partner technical contacts (SRE/Platform)
- Partner product owners / account teams
- Internal partner success and escalation contacts

Topline summary (one-paragraph to send at T+0):
We are aware of a regional request queueing issue affecting requests routed to our eu-west-2 region. Some partner integrations may see higher request latencies and intermittent 5xx throttling. Our operations team has identified an overloaded routing tier behind a temporary rate-limiting mismatch and is actively applying capacity adjustments and a prioritized fallback rule. No customer data has been lost. We will provide an update within 60 minutes and a full customer-facing post-incident summary within 48 hours.

Suggested customer email / message (concise):
Subject: Brief update — Increased latency for requests in eu-west-2
Hi <Partner name>,

We’re currently investigating increased request latency and intermittent failures affecting traffic routed through our eu-west-2 region. Some requests may queue for longer than normal; retries may succeed. Our engineers are applying routing and capacity mitigations now and we expect visible improvement within the next 30–60 minutes.

What you might see:
- Elevated P95/P99 latencies for text generation and chat endpoints
- Occasional 5xx responses and client-side timeouts
- No change to stored data or embeddings; no exposure of customer data

Immediate actions (recommended for partner teams):
- If you use regional pinning, consider temporarily routing non-critical traffic to a different region (e.g., eu-central-1) until we confirm recovery.
- Implement exponential backoff on retries (recommended max 3 attempts within 10s) to reduce duplicate load.
- If you require higher resilience, enable our cross-region fallback flag on the integration (we can toggle this for you).

We’re on it. We’ll share another update within 60 minutes and a full incident summary within 48 hours. If you need an urgent, dedicated update, reply and we’ll escalate.

Technical summary (short, for partners who want details):
- Root cause (current understanding): A recent change in routing rate-limit thresholds combined with a traffic burst from a large tenant resulted in persistent queueing at the routing tier (request broker) for eu-west-2. The broker’s per-shard admission policy caused requests to accumulate while lower-priority background jobs and a health-check storm consumed available worker slots.
- Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Increased routing broker worker pool for eu-west-2; 2) Temporarily relaxed per-tenant admission thresholds for tiered customers; 3) Enabled prioritized fallback routing for registered partners to alternative regions; 4) Deployed a short-term health-check backoff to reduce noise.
- Next steps in investigation: 1) Full audit of the recent routing threshold change (PR #3781); 2) Replay traffic to validate broker behavior under controlled load; 3) Add per-shard memory and queue depth metrics to the public metrics surface; 4) Follow-up change to health-check cadence and stronger protection for tenant bursts.

Customer-facing post-incident summary outline (to be delivered within 48 hours):
1) What happened — plain language timeline of events
2) Impact — which customers/regions were affected, estimated duration and scope
3) Root cause analysis — technical root cause and contributing factors
4) Immediate actions taken — who did what and when
5) Preventative changes planned — code/config changes, monitoring additions, runbook updates, timeline for enforcement
6) Compensation/SLA considerations — if applicable, how to request credits
7) Contacts and escalation routes

Operational checklist for partner operations / AM before sending:
- Confirm partner list and region mapping (who is pinned to eu-west-2).
- Verify partner-specific fallbacks are available and can be enabled quickly.
- Coordinate with SRE to confirm expected recovery window before sending (we need an ops sign-off).
- Include a clear escalation instruction and dedicated contact (phone or Slack) for high-impact partners.

FAQs to include in partner outreach:
Q: Will my data be affected?
A: No. This was a request routing and queueing issue. There is no evidence of data loss or corruption.

Q: Should we retry requests?
A: Yes, but use conservative exponential backoff (3 attempts) to avoid amplifying load. If you see repeated 5xx responses, switch to your configured fallback region.

Q: Can you force my traffic to another region?
A: For partners with cross-region fallback enabled, we can flip the routing flag temporarily. For others, we can work with you to update DNS/region pinning per your integration.

Q: Will this trigger an SLA credit?
A: We will evaluate impact based on affected requests and duration. Partners wishing to request compensation should open a support ticket referencing incident OPS-9876 and include request volume metrics. We will include guidance on the credit process in the 48-hour post-incident report.

Post-incident partner follow-up plan (48–72 hours):
- Draft and send the customer-facing post-incident report (SLA and RCA summarized in plain language).
- Offer a 1:1 technical review session for affected partners to walk through what happened and review mitigations.
- Provide a timeline for permanent fixes and monitor for recurrence for 30 days.
- If requested, prioritize a partner-specific compensatory review with commercial/account teams.

Internal notes for SRE and engineering partners:
- Primary ticket: JIRA OPS-9876 (routing queueing eu-west-2)
- Relevant PRs: routing-config PR#3781, broker-scaling PR#3792
- Playbook run: /ops/regional-queueing-playbook (use emergency scaling path A)
- Required postmortem owners: eng-servetime (lead), eng-routing (secondary), cs-partners (communication lead)

Tone guidance for message senders:
- Keep it short and factual; avoid blaming or speculative language.
- Prioritize what the partner needs to know to make an operational decision (retry strategy, fallback options, expected recovery window).
- Offer a clear escalation path and a named contact.

Template variants (short, technical, and executive):
- Short (one-line) update for status pages and channel notifications
- Technical note with metrics for partner SREs (include P50/P95/P99 charts and recent request volumes)
- Executive summary for partner account leads (impact, ETA, next steps, ask)

Example short status page blurb (to post publicly):
We are investigating increased request latencies and intermittent errors affecting traffic routed to eu-west-2. Engineers are applying routing and capacity mitigations; improvements expected within 60 minutes. No data loss.

Owner and escalation contacts (for partner teams to use):
- Primary: Aisha Patel (Partner Success Lead) — aisha@redwood.ai — pager: +1-415-555-0123
- Engineering SRE on-call: Samir Khan — samir@redwood.ai — Slack: @samir-k (ops channel)

Notes and follow-ups (internal):
- Ensure a post-incident retro is scheduled within 7 days and that the partner-specific RCA is shared with any impacted account owners.
- Add a monitoring alert that triggers when per-tenant queue depth exceeds 75% of configured admission threshold for >5 minutes.
- Track partner outreach in the incident log (OPS-9876) and attach sent messages and timestamps.

Appendix: canned snippets for quick copy/paste
- "Routing broker worker pool increased; temporary admission relaxations applied; prioritized fallback enabled for registered partners."
- "We recommend enabling cross-region fallback and applying exponential backoff (3 retries) until you receive our recovery confirmation."

End of template.

Notes: keep this file as the canonical partner outreach template for regional queueing events; update linked PR/Runbook IDs after postmortem.
